assignment:
Your principal is reconsidering the school's cell phone policy. She is considering two possible policies: 
Policy 1: Allow students to bring phones to school and use them during lunch periods and other free times, as long as the phones are turned off during class time. 
Policy 2: Do not allow students to have phones at school at all.
Write a letter to your principal convincing her which policy you believe is better. Support your position with specific reasons.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I heard your trying to decide between two cell phone policys. I think you should pick Policy 1, where we can bring our phones and use them at lunch and free time but we have to keep them off during class.

My first reason is safety. Alot of parents want to be able to get ahold of their kids during the day. Sometimes students need to call home too, like if practice gets canceled or there ride doesnt show up. If phones were totally banned we couldnt do that. And if there was ever a real emergency it would be really important to call our family fast.

My second reason is Policy 1 still keeps class time for learning. The phones have to be off in class anyway so teachers still get our attention. Taking our phones away at lunch doesnt help anything in the classroom. It just punishes kids on there own time.

Another reason is that a ban would be really hard to enforce. Kids are still going to sneak phones in their pockets and backpacks, trust me. Then teachers would waste time looking for phones instead of teaching us. If the rule is fair more students will actually follow it.

Last, Policy 1 teaches us to be responsible. When we get older and go to college or get a job nobody is going to take our phones away. We have to learn when to put them down on our own. Letting us practice at school helps get us ready for that.

So for all of these reasons I think you should choose Policy 1. It keeps classes focused and its fair to students too.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
essay_2:
Dear Principal,

I know you are trying to pick between two cell phone policies, and I think Policy 1 is the best choice. Students should be allowed to bring phones and use them at lunch and free time, as long as they are turned off in class.

The first reason is safety. Lots of parents want to be able to reach their kids during the day. Students also need a way to call home if practice gets canceled, if their ride falls through, or if something bad happens. Banning phones would take that away. In a real emergency, being able to call your family fast is really important, because being stuck and scared with no help is a terrible feeling.

Second, Policy 1 already protects class time, which is the whole point of a ban. If phones have to be off during class, teachers still get our attention. Taking them away at lunch would be useless for learning. It just punishes students during time that is supposed to be ours, and that feels very unfair.

Third, a full ban would be hard to enforce. Kids are still going to sneak phones in their pockets and backpacks. Then teachers would waste time searching for phones instead of teaching, which is a big problem and a really annoying fight for everyone. A simple rule that makes sense is easier to follow, and students will actually respect it and be happy with it.

Last, Policy 1 teaches responsibility. After we graduate, our bosses and professors will expect us to handle our own phones at a job or in college. We have to learn when to put them down ourselves. Practicing that at school is a good way to get ready for the real world.

For all these reasons, please choose Policy 1. It keeps class focused and still respects our safety and freedom.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
